study_id: Singh et al. - 2025 - Predicting post-lung transplant survival in systemic sclerosis using CT-derived features from preope

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: Although the study involves adult lung transplant recipients and uses deep learning for image segmentation, the survival prediction relies on Cox regression (a linear model) rather than a non‑linear AI predictive algorithm, thus failing the intervention criterion.

identification_methods.Setting: Single center, University of Pittsburgh Medical Center
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective cohort study of 102 systemic sclerosis patients who underwent lung transplantation between 2004 and 2020, using preoperative chest CT scans.
identification_methods.Institution: Department of Radiology, University of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Preoperative chest CT scans and clinical data from University of Pittsburgh Medical Center
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adults with systemic sclerosis, pre‑operative chest CT available, and lung transplant performed at UPMC between 2004–2020.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: 3‑D convolutional neural networks (Unet architecture) for automatic segmentation and feature extraction
identification_methods.Comparator: Traditional clinical/demographic models without CT‑derived features
identification_methods.Input Variables: Demographics, clinical variables (e.g., ACCI, tracheostomy, calcinosis, PAH), five CT‑derived body composition features and three cardiopulmonary CT features
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Features with missing values were excluded from analysis; no imputation performed
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Cox proportional hazards regression with backward stepwise selection; performance evaluated using ROC‑AUC, c-index, Brier score; 5‑fold CV applied to all models.

population.Inclusion criteria: SSc diagnosis, availability of chest CT imaging prior to LTx, and LTx due to SSc complications
population.Target Population: Systemic sclerosis patients undergoing lung transplantation
population.Population Notes: Retrospective single-center cohort from University of Pittsburgh (2004-2020), IRB approved, 49% mortality during follow-up

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: 3-D convolutional neural networks (CNN) with classic Unet architecture
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Automated segmentation and quantification of five body composition tissues and three cardiopulmonary structures using 3‑D CNN Unet models
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Post‑lung transplant survival at 1, 3 and 5 years (ROC‑AUC)
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: CT‑features model achieved AUCs of 0.77 (1 yr), 0.85 (3 yr) and 0.86 (5 yr); aggregate model achieved AUC 0.90 at 5 yr
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: CT‑derived features improved prediction over demographic and clinical models; best performance in 5‑year survival
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (ROC‑AUC)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All systemic sclerosis lung transplant recipients (n = 102)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: ROC‑AUC calculated via 5‑fold cross‑validation on pre‑transplant CT features
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: CT‑features model outperformed traditional models for 1‑year survival prediction
